title: Added summer land-surface heat: formerly redlined neighborhoods vs. non-redlined neighborhoods nearby (degrees Fahrenheit)
time_coverage: 2020 study (based on 1930s HOLC redlining maps vs. present-day land surface temperature)

source.name: The Effects of Historical Housing Policies on Resident Exposure to Intra-Urban Heat: A Study of 108 US Urban Areas
source.publisher: Hoffman, Shandas & Pendleton, journal 'Climate' (MDPI), Portland State University

notes: Peer-reviewed 2020 study comparing present-day land surface temperatures inside 1930s HOLC 'redlined' (D-grade) districts against non-redlined districts in the same 108 US urban areas: redlined areas ran about 5 degrees F hotter on average (up to 12.6 degrees F in the most extreme cities -- Portland OR, Denver CO, Minneapolis MN), a pattern consistent across 94% of the areas studied.
